pages.title: The friends who stayed
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The friends who stayed
Robin had met Moon after the breakup. The boy she knew
could be funny, sharp, infuriatingly stubborn—and then
suddenly absent in the middle of a conversation. A year
sounded like enough time to her. She wanted her friend back,
without quite understanding who he had been before she
arrived.
Tuly knew the part Robin had missed. She had watched Moon
and Rouhi turn ordinary afternoons into occasions, had heard
the easy laughter that needed no explanation. To her, Moon
was more than the friend who could not move on. He was the
boy she treated like a brother, trying to live inside a future
that no longer existed.
Neither woman knew how to mend that. Robin pushed; Tuly
made room. Sometimes both approaches hurt. Yet they kept
finding him after class, saving him a place, expecting him to
answer. Their friendship did not end when his mood changed.
For a few minutes beneath the trees, Moon could still meet
them there. Then a thought slipped between one joke and the
next. Tuly recognized the silence before he found a way to
apologize for it.
02

pages.title: A new face
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A new face
Lily entered the room expecting unfamiliar names, new faces
and an interesting class. Most people looked up. One young
man did not. His distance caught her attention precisely
because it seemed out of place among the small stir her
arrival had caused.
Curiosity came easily to Lily; cruelty did not. Her first teasing
question lost its lightness as Tuly answered. There was a
difference between someone being quiet and someone
carrying a story he had stopped expecting other people to
hear.
She settled beside Tuly. Only then did the teacher begin the
lesson. The idea of another universe belonged, for the
moment, to a classroom: a possibility to examine, not a fact to
believe. A passage through spacetime remained hypothetical.
Familiar people living unfamiliar lives were an invitation to
imagine.
Moon listened. Questions about the universe could still pull
him out of himself. Lily noticed that change too—the way his
attention returned when there was something large enough to
wonder about.
04

pages.title: Someone willing to listen
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Someone willing to listen
Lily asked for the story, not a performance of being fine. Her
directness startled Moon, but she waited for his agreement.
He did not have to defend the fact that it still mattered.
Across the canteen table she became quieter. The playful
confidence that had carried her through a new classroom gave
way to attention. Robin and Tuly went to collect food, leaving
him enough space to choose a beginning.
There were many ways to describe a breakup. He could have
begun with the argument, the unanswered hope, the marriage.
None explained why the loss still occupied so much of his life.
He began with happiness. Before Lily could understand the
person he had become, she would need to know the future he
had once expected. Plates clattered at the next table. Across
from him, she waited while he found his way back to an
ordinary afternoon with Rouhi.

pages.title: When there was always tomorrow
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
When there was always
tomorrow
Happiness had not looked extraordinary while they were living
it. It had looked like someone slowing down to match his
stride, a book left open because neither of them could stop
laughing, the certainty that a familiar face would be waiting
after class.
Tuly had been there. That was why she could not reduce his
grief to stubbornness. She remembered the ease between
them, and the way they spoke about marriage as if it were a
place already marked on a map.
Moon believed a future could be secured by working hard
enough. Rouhi wanted a place in the life he was living while he
worked toward it. At the time, those wishes seemed to fit
together without effort.
Across a table in the present, Moon remembered the warmth
first. He could still hear how lightly she had asked him not to
forget her. Memory had given the sentence a weight it had not
carried that afternoon.
08

pages.title: The space between promises
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The space between promises
Moon’s effort was real. So was the absence it created. He
could account for every unfinished project and approaching
deadline, but not for the accumulating hours in which Rouhi
waited for him to have room for her.
She knew he was under pressure. That knowledge became
another reason to postpone speaking. The problems at home
did not disappear because she kept them out of his day; they
simply became hers to carry alone.
He understood his work as an act of commitment. She
experienced its repeated interruptions as distance. Neither
meaning cancelled the other. The same future that justified his
busyness could not comfort her in every lonely present.
Mir and Jaffar occupied some of the space he left. Their
presence did not create every problem between the couple. It
gave them access to a relationship already struggling to hear
itself.

pages.title: Words that arrive too quickly
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Words that arrive too quickly
By the time Rouhi spoke, she had already spent months living
with the question. Moon encountered it all at once. He heard
the end of their future before he understood the exhaustion
that had brought her there.
He wanted a problem he could solve. A decision she had
reached without him felt like proof that she had stopped
believing in everything he was trying to build. The possibility
that she had been waiting for him to notice her pain arrived
too late for the first answer.
Anger gave him words quickly. Understanding would take
longer.
When she walked away, he mistook his own certainty for hers.
He could not imagine the space between them remaining
empty. He waited for the familiar turn of her head, the
conversation beginning again. It did not.

pages.title: The day he finally listened
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The day he finally listened
The call gave him facts he should have known before the
breakup. More difficult than the facts was the way she spoke
them: without the argument he had prepared to answer.
He would have tried to help. He believed that, and the belief
was sincere. Yet she had spent months searching for a
moment when bringing him her problems would not feel like
adding to a burden he already carried.
Being willing to listen, he began to understand, was different
from making someone feel able to speak.
There was no single sentence that could repair those months.
The conversation explained the distance without closing it.
Moon had reached the place where he could hear her, and
found that she was no longer asking him to stay.
14

pages.title: What silence allowed
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
What silence allowed
In the telling, Moon returned to moments he had once passed
over. Mir’s comments had found a ready wound: the feeling
that a promised future was being used to excuse a lonely
present.
Rouhi did not need her unhappiness invented for her. That
was what made the interference effective. Doubt already
existed; Mir kept giving it a sharper voice.
Jaffar’s part was quieter. Moon remembered the greetings
that had remained ordinary while important knowledge went
unspoken. He understood that silence afterward as a choice
made in someone else’s interest.
Remembering their interference did not spare Moon his own
regret. Rouhi had been hurting, and he had failed to see
enough of it. Other people had found advantages in the
distance between them. He was left trying to separate what
they had done from what he wished he had done differently.
16

pages.title: A future ends on the telephone
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A future ends on the
telephone
Waiting gave his changed habits a direction. He imagined
Rouhi seeing the difference, imagined the conversation in
which both of them admitted that the story was unfinished.
Hope could make the silence feel temporary.
Tuly stayed beside him through those months. Robin came to
know him in that period, when the earlier happiness was
already something other people described. Neither could
make the decision he wanted arrive.
The marriage call closed a future he had continued
rehearsing. Jaffar’s name made the loss more bewildering, but
the deepest shock was simpler: the life Moon was still waiting
to begin had ended for her.
Faith remained a place where he could speak without
pretending to be composed. After prayer, he asked Allah for
help with pain he could not reason away. Nothing about that
plea made grief orderly. It gave him somewhere to bring it.

pages.title: Before the impossible question
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Before the impossible
question
Lily had been eager to ask when they first sat down. Now she
understood why eagerness alone was not enough. Some
answers changed the question that should follow.
Moon was not asking to intrude on Rouhi’s marriage. The
person he missed belonged to the shared life before its
end—the woman who had believed in him, and the version of
himself who had believed that being loved meant there would
always be another chance.
Lily let that distinction settle. Her silence was attentive, not
empty. She turned the thought over before offering it back in
the language that had brought them into the same classroom.
It was an impossible question, safely hypothetical. At least,
that was how it sounded when she asked. Neither of them yet
had a reason to be afraid of the answer.
20

pages.title: An absence in the air
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
An absence in the air
Moon answered before he could make the answer smaller. A
life he knew was over could still summon a certainty that the
present rarely offered him. Lily had asked about a possibility,
and for a moment he allowed himself to inhabit it.
Then the room acquired an absence. Tables, chairs, the light
across the floor—all remained ordinary around a small
darkness that reflected none of them. Its white ripples
seemed to disturb the air without disturbing anyone else.
Lily followed his attention and found a different explanation.
Rouhi was there with Jaffar. What she recognized was the
reason a young man might stop in the middle of a sentence.
She had no reason to imagine that they were looking into the
same aisle and seeing different things.
Moon could barely hold those two realities together: the
woman whose life had continued without him, and the
impossible shape that had interrupted his own. By the time
he looked again, only the familiar room remained. The empty
air offered no reassurance. It gave him nothing he could
show another person.
22

pages.title: The room carries on
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The room carries on
Their friends returned to a conversation that seemed easy to
recognize. Moon had been talking about Rouhi again. Robin’s
exasperation belonged to that familiar story; Tuly’s question
made space for an answer she thought she understood.
He let them believe it. Explaining the darkness would mean
asking them to accept something he could not account for
himself. The image was clear in his memory, yet already the
ordinary room was making it difficult to trust.
Lily had heard more than the others. Still, she had seen only
Rouhi and Jaffar across the canteen. Moon could not tell
whether her calm made the event less frightening or made
his isolation more complete.
Lunch gave everyone something to do with their hands.
Conversation moved on, plates shifted, another group passed
the windows. Moon answered when spoken to. Underneath
those small tasks, one question continued without an
audience. What he had seen was gone; the fact that he had
seen it would not leave him.
24

pages.title: A theory with consequences
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
PRESENT / NEXT CLASS
Suppose the multiverse exists. In the
hypothetical model we’re discussing,
matter from different universes
cannot safely coexist. Their matter
and ours differ. They vibrate at one
frequency; we vibrate at another.
If matter from another universe
entered ours and came into contact
with our matter, that conflict could
start a chain reaction. Something
small could lead to mass destruction,
like a butterfly effect.
There is also another theory: different
branches of a timeline create
different universes, each moving at
its own vibration.
Then, sir, is it possible for matter
from two different universes to live
together, but on a different timeline?
We don’t know. But maybe it is
possible. Who knows? Science is
fascinating in its own way.

pages.title: A theory with consequences
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A theory with consequences
In class, the impossible had rules again. A thought
experiment could be held at a safe distance, questioned,
revised, and left on the board when the lesson ended. Moon
tried to give it the same attention he always had.
The teacher distinguished the model from established
knowledge. Within this imagined account, matter from
different universes might not remain compatible. A tiny
meeting could have consequences larger than the place
where it began. The proposal invited questions; it did not
settle them.
Lily listened for the edge of the argument. If the trouble
came from different universes sharing one place, what might
change on another timeline? It was the sort of question she
liked: one that found a doorway in an explanation instead of
accepting its walls.
Moon had a question he did not ask. Nothing in the lecture
proved that the darkness in the canteen belonged to the
subject on the board. Yet he could no longer hear the
discussion as entirely remote from his life. An abstract
possibility had acquired a shape only he remembered seeing.

pages.title: Only Moon can see it
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Only Moon can see it
The lesson followed them into the corridor. Lily could turn a
difficult idea around with delight, and Moon answered with
an enthusiasm his friends had not heard often enough lately.
For a moment there was nothing to explain about his
expression.
Her next question brought Rouhi into the possibility.
Somewhere, perhaps, a different decision had led to a
different life. Moon knew it was speculation. Knowing that
did little to weaken the feeling it awakened.
The darkness returned in open space ahead of him. Its
distance mattered: nothing touched his face or his hands,
nothing lay on the floor. It occupied the air as distinctly as
the corridor occupied the building. White ripples trembled
around a surface that gave back no light.
His friends watched him. Their attention moved with his
alarm, never with the thing that caused it. Lily searched
where he indicated and found no object to name. Moon had
wanted someone else to confirm the world he was looking at.
Instead, their worried faces made its solitude unmistakable.

pages.title: The promise on his wrist
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The promise on his wrist
Robin’s impatience reached him more readily than anyone’s
concern. She wanted the memories to lose their authority.
Moon heard another reminder that Rouhi’s life no longer
waited for his understanding or consent.
At home, the watch made remembering almost effortless. It
was useful, ordinary, still part of the movement of his day.
That was why the promise attached to it could arrive without
warning. A gift given outdoors on an earlier afternoon had
outlasted the future spoken over it.
He did not remember a perfect relationship. He remembered
the certainty with which he had expected another chance to
become possible. Regret kept presenting him with a life
altered by one answer, one conversation, one decision made
differently.
The room answered with nothing he knew how to
understand. Near its far corner, away from the bed, the same
darkness occupied empty air. The watch remained solid
against his wrist. Moon looked from that familiar weight
toward a thing he could not touch or explain, and found that
wishing no longer felt private.
30

pages.title: A long night
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A long night
Moon tried the smallest experiment he could think of. If he
stopped looking, perhaps the room would return to itself. He
counted carefully, as though accuracy might make a
difference to something that had ignored every other rule he
knew.
The darkness did not oblige him. It stayed in the same
remote corner, with enough space around it to make its
position painfully clear. He could look away from it, but doing
so felt like leaving a question unattended.
Hours lost their useful divisions. The watch recorded them;
his attention did not. Fear gave way to exhaustion and then
returned whenever his eyes opened. Morning changed the
color of the walls without changing what stood apart from
them.
By noon he had become less certain of himself than of the
shape. It had survived the explanations he tried to give it. He
needed another person in the room—not to solve the
universe, only to look toward the corner and tell him whether
the same world was still there for both of them.

pages.title: Two views of one corner
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Two views of one corner
The arrival of his friends gave the room back some of its
ordinary scale. Robin filled the doorway with instructions,
annoyance, the practical certainty that getting him outside
would help. Moon almost welcomed the familiar pressure.
Tuly stayed when Robin turned to leave. Her concern was
less easy to dismiss because it asked him for an answer. He
could tell her where to look. He could not make the answer
appear there for her.
The corner remained the same corner: the window, the edge
of the wall, the stretch of open air above the floor. From
Moon’s place, a darkness held its position within it. From
Tuly’s, there was only a room in daylight.
She believed that something was wrong without believing
she could see what he saw. For Moon, that distinction offered
little comfort. For Tuly, the practical question was how to
bring her friend back into a day they could share. Neither
understood the distance opening between those two kinds of
care.

pages.title: What makes it leave
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
What makes it leave
Tuly reached for the history they both knew. She had listened
to Moon promise that Rouhi would come back, had watched
him make a home for that hope while months passed around
it. She wanted the present to become harder for him to avoid.
The words hurt because they were not new. He had
answered them many times in private, and never found an
answer that stopped them hurting. For a moment, the life he
longed for lost its hold over the life he remembered losing.
Then the corner was empty.
Moon had no explanation for the timing. Tuly saw a pause in
his attention and continued making the day practical: friends
downstairs, a movie, a reason to get dressed and leave the
room. She could not know that her reminder had coincided
with a change in something she had never seen.
He agreed to come. Relief made room for another question. If
the darkness could stay through a whole night and vanish in
the middle of one conversation, perhaps the conversation
mattered. It was not a conclusion yet. It was the first detail
he felt able to carry out of the room.
36

pages.title: A question without ridicule
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A question without ridicule
By the time Lily found him, Moon had learned to make his
worry sound smaller. He expected impatience before it
arrived. Saying nothing seemed easier than watching another
friend search his face for a sensible explanation.
Lily’s persistence carried a different tone. She was playful
enough to make room for embarrassment, but she did not
mistake his reluctance for an invitation to leave. The question
stayed open without becoming an accusation.
Moon needed that small permission. Not permission to
believe every frightening possibility, but permission to
describe what had happened before someone decided what it
meant. The distinction let him begin.
Around the bench, campus life continued at its usual
distance. No darkness interrupted the air. Nothing
announced that the conversation mattered. Lily leaned
toward a friend with something difficult to say, and Moon
tried, once more, to make his private experience into words
another person could follow.

pages.title: The thought before the darkness
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The thought before the
darkness
Once he began, Moon discovered that the events had a
sequence. A place, a thought, the appearance of the
darkness; another person unable to see it; then, sometimes,
its disappearance. Describing those pieces made them less
like one uninterrupted fear.
Lily resisted the temptation to name the thing immediately.
She asked about what came before it. An answer to that
question would not explain the object, but it might reveal
whether its arrivals were as arbitrary as they felt.
Moon searched the memories carefully. Each had begun with
a life he wanted: Rouhi choosing him, a second chance
accepted, happiness continuing beyond the point where it
had ended here. The longing was familiar. The darkness was
new.
They had a possible pattern, nothing more. Lily’s interest
helped him hold it without turning it into certainty. For the
first time since the canteen, another person was examining
the experience beside him. Even without seeing what he saw,
she had made it less lonely to look.

pages.title: The other half of the pattern
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The other half of the pattern
Remembering the arrivals had made the darkness seem
almost generous. Remembering its departures changed that.
The interruptions had come when longing gave way to the
facts he least wanted to revisit.
Tuly’s words returned with the clarity of an injury. She had
been trying to help him face the present. Moon had felt the
old loss again, and the corner had become empty. Robin’s
remarks belonged to the same painful pattern.
Lily considered the connection without pretending it
explained everything. A repeated sequence could suggest a
cause; it could also mislead them. They had only his
memories, and neither knew what the object was.
Still, the possibility altered Moon’s fear. Something he had
experienced as an invasion now seemed to answer a
movement within him. That did not make it safe. It made it
personal. The thought was frightening in a new way, but it
also restored a curiosity he recognized as his own. He and
Lily sat a little straighter, like two students who had found a
question the classroom had not yet taught them to ask.

pages.title: The shape of a wish
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The shape of a wish
Remembered from class: “In our hypothetical model, different
universes may follow different timelines. Something that has happened
in one may not have happened in another.”
The idea of different timelines stayed with Moon after class.
There was comfort in imagining a possibility untouched by
the choices that had closed his own future. He knew the
difference between an idea and a promise, but longing was
not careful about the boundary.
Lily’s teasing gave that possibility a domestic shape: a
second chance, a marriage, an ordinary life together. Her
warmth made it easy to smile. Moon did, and for a moment
the imagined life felt close enough to remember.
The darkness returned ahead of him in the plaza. His friends
noticed his attention change before they noticed anything in
the air. Lily recognized the look and asked the question they
had learned to share.
This time the answer would not fit the old pattern. The small
absence was becoming a vertical interruption in the world,
tall enough for a person. Within it there seemed to be depth
without distance, a room that did not belong to the buildings
around them. Moon stopped trying to compare it with what
had happened before. Someone was inside.

pages.title: Two impossible truths
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Two impossible truths
The plaza became a place to brace against. Rain struck at an
angle, branches strained, and the familiar buildings
disappeared behind a weather that had arrived too quickly.
The tear remained upright in the air, dark and impossibly
still within the violence around it.
The woman reaching through it knew his name. Her
desperation belonged to someone who had been searching,
not someone surprised to find a stranger. Moon recognized
Rouhi before he could decide what recognition meant.
Lily’s protest forced him to look away. Far across the plaza,
the Rouhi of this world stood beside Jaffar in her blush dress.
She was as shocked as they were. The distance between the
two women did not resolve the contradiction; it made it
undeniable.
Moon looked back toward the opening. The other Rouhi was
crying for him with a grief he did not yet understand. She
wore a different life as plainly as she wore a different dress.
The storm gave him no quiet in which to think. There was
only the hand reaching out, and the knowledge that the
woman beyond it was afraid he would not come.

pages.title: Beyond their reach
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Beyond their reach
The distance to her was only a few steps. The wind made
each one a decision. Moon could hear his friends calling, but
their voices came from a place his attention had already left.
Tuly knew how to reach him in an ordinary moment. She
could step into his line of sight, touch his shoulder, insist that
he answer. Here, the space between them had become
physical resistance. Robin’s alarm stripped every trace of
impatience from her voice.
Rouhi’s hand remained ahead of him. Moon did not have an
explanation for the other world, or a plan for what would
happen if he crossed the remaining distance. The need in her
face had arrived before either could exist.
He leaned into the storm. Behind him were people who
wanted him safe; in front of him was someone who seemed to
have waited through a different kind of catastrophe. He could
not make those demands agree. He could only keep moving
toward the hand he had once believed he would never hold
again.

pages.title: A hand made real
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
A hand made real
Contact did not calm the storm. It made one thing certain
within it. Her hand resisted his with the weight and warmth
of a living person, and the distance that had seemed
impossible became something his body could fight.
Moon pulled. Rouhi trusted the motion before she could see
where it would leave her. For an instant their separate griefs
had only one task: keep hold.
The embrace came before any explanation. Neither waited to
ask which world had sent her, or why a passage had
answered a wish. They held one another with the urgency of
people who had each learned that an ordinary goodbye could
be the last.
Light emptied the opening behind them. The weather began
to loosen its grip, slowly enough that the last rain still caught
in their clothes. Moon’s friends remained a few steps away,
unwilling to interrupt and unable to understand.
Against his shoulder, Rouhi wept with relief. Moon had
imagined seeing her happy with him again. He had never
imagined being the person whose return someone else had
prayed for.

pages.title: The lives left outside the embrace
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The lives left outside the
embrace
Across the plaza, Jaffar looked at the woman beside him as if
the answer might be written on her face. Rouhi had no
answer. Shock left room for something more painful: the
sight of a happiness that seemed to have survived
somewhere beyond the choices she knew.
Neither could enter the reunion unfolding at a distance. It
belonged to a history they had not lived. Their own history
remained between them, suddenly difficult to speak about.
Closer to Moon, his friends faced a different bewilderment.
Tuly knew both the joy before the breakup and the long year
afterward. Robin had known only the aftermath. Lily had
asked a question she thought could remain hypothetical.
Each had a different reason to struggle with the same sight.
Moon finally found room for a question. It was smaller than
the impossibility around him: how? Rouhi held him as though
letting go might undo everything. When she began to answer,
the story moved away from the plaza and into the life she had
brought with her.

pages.title: The life on the other side
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The life on the other side
In Rouhi’s world, the difficult conversation had not been the
last one. Moon had asked for another chance, and she had
given him an answer that changed the life they would share.
The difference was not an absence of problems. It was a
decision to remain and face them together.
Her family’s refusal made that decision costly. Love did not
remove the pressure around them. It gave her a reason to
choose whose future she was willing to build, and what
uncertainty she could bear in making it.
Marriage returned them to ordinary time. A room to come
home to. Meals interrupted by laughter. Small habits that
became familiar enough to pass unnoticed. Happiness lived
in those repetitions, not in a permanent escape from
difficulty.
As she remembered, Rouhi spoke to the man in front of her
with the intimacy of someone who had known those days.
Moon listened to a life he had wished for and never lived.
Her certainty made it real for him, and made the grief
waiting behind it harder to imagine.

pages.title: The road home
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The road home
The day had been ordinary enough to make an ordinary
expectation feel safe. Moon was coming home. Rouhi’s mind
had a place for the sound of his arrival, for whatever small
conversation would begin when he entered.
The accident broke that expectation before it became a
memory. An afternoon road, a journey almost completed, the
sudden interruption of a life that still contained plans for
later. There was no preparation that could make the news fit
the day in which she received it.
Afterward, familiar objects became difficult to look at. A cup
could hold the shape of a habit; an empty chair could make
absence visible. The apartment had not changed enough to
account for the fact that he would not return to it.
In the plaza of another world, Rouhi told Moon that he had
died. The words belonged to her life with a certainty his own
continued breathing could not undo. He could hear her grief
and see what she had endured. He could not remember the
goodbye she had been forced to survive.

pages.title: Months without an answer
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Months without an answer
Grief changed the scale of time. Months passed, but a room
could still return her to the first morning without him. Other
people could measure the distance from the accident. Rouhi
lived with its arrival again and again.
Prayer gave her somewhere to bring the longing. She
returned to the mat through daylight and darkness, asking
Allah for what she could not stop wanting. Exhaustion
accumulated in her face, in the weight of her shoulders, in
the effort it took to rise and begin another day.
When her strength finally failed, she had no witness. The
room held its ordinary objects around her: the mat, the
window, the empty corner. The darkness appeared at a
distance immediately after she collapsed, small enough that
it changed no furniture and large enough to change what
waking meant.
She did not know what it was. Belief reached for a meaning
before understanding could supply one. To someone who had
continued asking for a way back, an impossible presence
could feel like the beginning of an answer. She watched it
with the frail attention of a person who could no longer
afford to dismiss hope.

pages.title: One moment, two worlds
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
One moment, two worlds
The two rooms did not share a clock or a view. Yet the
changes were paired. When the small darkness became
visible to Moon, the white waves around Rouhi’s void
brightened. The light belonged to its boundary; the center
stayed perfectly black.
When Moon’s painful memories drew the object out of his
sight, the light in Rouhi’s room faded. The black core
remained there. She could continue watching it even when
his world offered him only empty air.
Neither had the other half of this pattern. Moon was learning
what preceded the appearances he could see. Rouhi was
learning how to wait through a light that returned and
retreated without explaining itself.
Across the two lives, longing had become a rhythm neither
could yet name. It was not a promise she could test or a rule
he could prove. But every return gave Rouhi another reason
to stay near the small absence in her room, and every
disappearance taught Moon that his thoughts might matter
to something outside himself.

MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The same opening, seen from
home
The light returned with a force Rouhi had not seen before.
The small darkness opened into a view, and the room she had
watched for so long became the edge of another place.
Moon stood beyond it in the storm, his friends behind him.
This was the same moment that had stopped them in the
plaza, seen from the other side. He looked astonished, alive,
close enough for hope to become movement.
Rouhi knew the danger of losing him better than she
understood the danger of reaching. The afternoon road, the
news, the months alone—all of it had made waiting into an
unbearable skill. When the opening finally showed him to
her, she could not continue practicing it.
Her account returned to the present in his arms. Moon could
now understand the urgency with which she had called his
name. She had not been trying to leave a stranger’s world for
an adventure. She had been trying to come home to a person,
and had recognized him before either universe offered an
explanation.

pages.title: For one breath
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
For one breath
The explanation did not make the reunion ordinary. It made
the joy easier to understand. Two people had reached the
same embrace from different losses, each carrying a version
of the other that had seemed beyond recovery.
Tuly watched without knowing where to put her questions.
Happiness for Moon arrived before certainty about anything
else. Robin stood quieter than he had ever seen her. Lily
could follow the story and still find herself astonished by the
people standing at its end.
For a breath, Moon allowed himself to look at Rouhi without
searching for what might take her away. Her happiness had
the openness of a child’s, made fragile by tears that had not
yet stopped. He met it with a tenderness too full for another
question.
The world gave them that breath. Then something shifted
beneath it.
The first crack was small enough to be mistaken for an old
fault in the paving. Its movement made that impossible. Joy
had brought all their attention close; the sound from the
ground forced it outward again.

A world where the sky should
be
The darkness returned without the weather. There were no
gathering clouds to make its arrival familiar. Light drained
from the plaza as something too large to belong in the sky
began to occupy it.
Continents, oceans, a curve that should have been visible
only from far away: another Earth approached through a vast
break above them. Energy spread around its boundary and
cast unfamiliar light over the buildings below. It had not
struck their world. The space between the two was already
becoming unbearable to look at.
The five of them had no distance from which to understand
the scale. A crack underfoot was immediate; the planet above
seemed beyond anything a person could respond to. Between
those facts stood the couple whose reunion had just felt like
the end of danger.
Moon held Rouhi closer without meaning to. She looked
upward beside him, as shocked as the friends who had
witnessed her arrival. Whatever was happening, it had not
been part of the hope she carried through the opening.

MULTIVERSAL LOVE
Maybe
Lily’s mind returned to the classroom because it was the only
place she had heard anything like an explanation. A model of
incompatible matter. A small contact with consequences
larger than its beginning. Branches of time that might obey
different conditions.
None of it had been established as the law of this event. She
knew that even as the pieces seemed to align. Fear made
certainty tempting; the people looking at her needed more
honesty than that.
She offered a possibility. Perhaps Rouhi’s presence had
joined things that could not remain together here. Perhaps
the spreading damage was the reaction the teacher’s model
had imagined. Saying it aloud made the implication
immediate: saving this world might require undoing the
reunion they had just witnessed.
Tuly asked the question no theory could make less urgent.
Lily did not know how to stop it. The thought of sending
Rouhi back gave them a direction to consider, not a method.
The sky kept changing while they stood close enough to hear
one another, trying to make a human decision inside a scale
that had stopped being human.

pages.title: No answer large enough
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
No answer large enough
The danger no longer waited in the sky alone. The plaza
shifted beneath their feet. Every new break made standing
still feel like a choice, yet none of them could point toward
safety with any confidence.
Moon looked at Rouhi and found no distance between love
and fear. He had spent a year imagining what he would give
for the chance to hold her again. Now the chance stood
beside him, and the cost seemed to be reaching people who
had never made that wish.
Rouhi had already lived through losing him. The possibility of
being sent away was not an abstract correction to her. It was
a return to an absence she had barely survived. She held him
without pretending that courage made the prospect easier.
Their friends stayed. They could not explain the sky or close
the cracks, but they could remain within reach of one
another. For a moment that was the only answer any of them
had: five people refusing to let fear turn them into strangers
while the place beneath them came apart.

pages.title: The question he can ask
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
The question he can ask
Moon held her face as if gentleness could give them time. He
had no plan to offer her. The damage around them made
every possible answer feel too late or too small.
Then the familiar darkness appeared in open air away from
them. It was small again, edged with white waves,
unchanged by the immense light above. Both saw it.
Something in Moon’s attention settled, though nothing in the
world became clear enough to explain.
He looked back at Rouhi. Whatever he believed the
appearance meant, he did not turn it into a promise he could
guarantee. There was one question he could ask without
pretending to understand the universe.
Her face was warm between his hands. He looked at her with
the care of someone holding what is most precious and most
vulnerable at once. Around them, their friends waited for an
instruction that did not come. Moon spoke only to Rouhi,
asking for trust in the space where neither of them had an
answer.

pages.title: With everything
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
With everything
Rouhi’s answer did not erase her fear. It existed beside it,
with all the grief that had brought her here. Trust was not
knowledge of what would happen next. It was the part of
herself she could still place in his hands.
Moon said nothing more. His pride in her was quiet and
painful, a tenderness that had no use for another promise.
When she held him, he accepted the embrace with the care
her answer deserved.
He looked once toward his friends. Tuly had known the
happiness he lost; Robin had stayed through the person he
became afterward; Lily had listened long enough to
recognize a question nobody else could see. They stood close
by, yet no words could make the moment easy to share.
The last thing he gave them was that look. Then his attention
returned to Rouhi, whose face was pressed against him as
though she had finally reached the place she had been
searching for. He closed his eyes. Above them, the light
gathered.

pages.title: After the light
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
After the light
Light reached the couple before anyone found another word.
For an instant the plaza had no edges, and the five people
within it were no longer visible to one another.
When the world returned, it returned with an impossible
calm. The sky was clear. The paving beneath the three
friends was whole. The approaching planet and the darkness
that had accompanied it were gone.
Lily, Robin and Tuly were on the ground. Awareness came
back in pieces: a hand against stone, the effort of sitting up,
the sound of another person breathing nearby. Their
surroundings offered none of the damage that should have
explained their fear.
Then they counted the people.
The space where Moon and Rouhi had stood was empty.
There was no opening to look through, no path across the
restored plaza that could tell them where to follow. Relief at
being alive gave way to a question the calm could not
answer. The world had recovered its familiar shape. Their
lives had not.

pages.title: And what about them?
pages.text:
MULTIVERSAL LOVE
And what about them?
Robin asked first because someone had to make the absence
into words. Tuly was already looking beyond the place they
had stood, as though Moon might answer from a distance too
ordinary for them to have considered.
Lily had the same pieces they did: the reunion, the damage,
the final embrace, the light. The explanation she offered was
a possibility shaped by grief. She could not verify where the
two had gone, or whether sacrifice was the right word for a
choice she had not understood in time.
Tuly’s question reached past the safety of the restored world.
What about the people who had just found one another?
What kind of answer could account for them without making
their love a small detail in everyone else’s survival?
Lily had none. Her silence held the limit of what she knew.
Beside her, Robin’s composure gave way, and Tuly stopped
searching long enough to feel the emptiness she had been
trying to outrun. The three of them remained together
because that was what their friendship had always asked of
them, even when staying offered no explanation.
